themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints surged to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1500% spike with z-score 5.67—suggesting either a coordinated event, holiday preparation, or emerging enforcement gap in St. George/Stapleton.
evidence: 4 illegal fireworks complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score 5.67, severity rated high—statistically extreme deviation
Timing suggests holiday-driven or event-driven catalyst worth investigating
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and Fire Marshal about what triggered this week's spike—is there a specific event or pattern?
Interview residents in St. George about noise and safety impact, particularly families and elderly neighbors
Investigate whether illegal fireworks sales are operating in the district and where enforcement is focused

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 24 THIS WEEK versus a 5.6 weekly average—a 327% spike with z-score 4.87—indicating either new nightlife activity, construction, or venue operations ramping up in the district.
evidence: 24 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.6 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Suggests new or expanded commercial activity or special event activity
reporting_angles: Map the 24 complaints geographically—are they concentrated near specific venues, construction sites, or new businesses?
Contact NYPD and Department of Environmental Protection about enforcement actions on commercial noise violators
Interview affected residents about which businesses or activities are driving the noise; cross-reference with new permits filed

themes_detail.label: Water Infrastructure Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK (700% above the 0.4 weekly baseline, z-score 5.42), while water system complaints hit 108 three weeks ago (150% above baseline, z-score 3.81), suggesting active drainage or pipe issues in St. George/Stapleton.
evidence: Standing water: 3 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score 5.42, 700% spike)
Water system: 108 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 43.2 weekly average (z-score 3.81, 150% spike)
Two converging water-related spikes suggest infrastructure vulnerability or recent failure
reporting_angles: Contact DEP about active water main breaks, drainage issues, or construction work in the district during the past 3 weeks
Map complaint locations to identify whether standing water and system failures are in the same neighborhoods
Interview residents about health and safety impacts (mold, flooding, water quality) and timeline of issues
Note: CB has requested DEP capital budget repeatedly—is this spike evidence of deferred maintenance?

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints (damaged and missing combined) totaled 11 across two weeks ago, representing 322% above the 1.3 weekly baseline—suggesting accelerated deterioration or weather-related damage to district wayfinding infrastructure.
evidence: Street sign damaged: 6 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score 4.5, 300% spike)
Street sign missing: 5 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score 4.18, 344% spike)
Combined signal suggests rapid deterioration or winter weather damage
reporting_angles: Verify whether this correlates with snowstorm or severe weather two weeks ago
Contact DOT about street sign repair backlogs—note CB's repeated requests for street light and infrastructure funding
Document locations of missing/damaged signs for wayfinding impact on navigation and safety

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints reached 6 complaints two weeks ago—a 300% spike from the 1.5 weekly baseline (z-score 3.67)—suggesting community friction around new or existing retail cannabis operations in the district.
evidence: 6 cannabis retailer complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (z-score 3.67, 300% spike)
Suggests new retail licenses issued or community organizing around existing operations
District has active land use applications and building permits—may indicate legal retail expansion
reporting_angles: Identify which cannabis retailer(s) triggered complaints—new openings or existing locations facing backlash?
Interview community members about specific concerns (odor, youth access, foot traffic, storefront visibility)
Cross-reference with DOH retail licenses and CEQR/land use applications in the district
